title: Reverse Hölder inequality for positive exponents
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $0<r<1$, and let $u,v$ be nonnegative real-valued functions on the Boolean cube $\\{0,1\\}^n$. Then their uniform inner product satisfies $\\langle u,v\\rangle \\ge M_r(u)M_{r/(r-1)}(v)$, where $M_p$ denotes the extended power mean.
replaced: Let $0<r<1$ and $u,v:\{0,1\}^n\to[0,\infty)$. Then $\E[uv]\ge M_r(u)M_{r/(r-1)}(v)$. For nonnegative functions $u$, the extended mean is $M_r(u)=(\E u^r)^{1/r}$ when $r>0$; the same formula applies for $r<0$ when $u$ is positive everywhere. For positive $u$, $M_0(u)=\exp(\E\log u)$; if $r\le0$ and $u$ has a zero, $M_r(u)=0$. All expectations are uniform.
